items: Getting to the start

The start is beside the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku. Shinjuku Station is huge and easy to get lost in: walk the route the day before, and allow 15–20 minutes from the station to security.
Race morning

You must enter through your assigned gate and start from your assigned corral; starting from another corral means disqualification. There is no race-day bib pickup, and bag check is only for runners who paid for it when entering.
The course
The first few kilometres run downhill, which makes it easy to start too fast. Several out-and-back sections have cut-off times, so check them in your runner guide.
Getting to the start

Official B.A.A. buses take runners from Boston Common to Hopkinton (about an hour); driving to Hopkinton is discouraged. There's no need to take the very first bus: you'll only wait longer in Athletes' Village.
Race morning
Athletes' Village is mostly open grass. Bring warm clothes you can throw away (they're collected and donated), something to sit on, and the breakfast you're used to.
The course

Boston drops about 140 m overall, and the early downhills tempt you to go out too fast. Save energy for the Newton Hills from around km 26, ending with Heartbreak Hill near km 33; the last 8 km are mostly downhill.
Getting to the start

The start is spread over several coloured assembly areas in Blackheath and Greenwich Park, each with its own station (Blackheath, Greenwich or Maze Hill). Your runner email names yours, and it can change from year to year. Runners travel free on race morning by showing their bib.
Race morning
Trains to the start get very busy from about 7 am. Each start area is a 10–15 minute walk from its station, so leave plenty of time. Bag drop is at the start.
The course
Flat and famous: past the Cutty Sark, over Tower Bridge near halfway, through Canary Wharf and along the Embankment to the finish on The Mall. Crowds are loud the whole way.
Getting to the start
The main start is beside the stadium in Green Point. Roads close from 5:30 am and private cars can't get near the start after 6:30 am, so walk, or take a MyCiTi bus if you're staying further away.
Watch the wind
Wind is the big unknown in Cape Town: the 2025 race was cancelled after strong overnight winds. Check the forecast and the organiser's messages the night before.
The course
A single, mostly rolling loop through Woodstock, Salt River, Rondebosch and the city centre, finishing along the Atlantic coast. Run in a group on the exposed coastal stretch to stay out of the wind.
Getting to the start

The start is in North Sydney by North Sydney Oval. Public transport is free with your bib. Depending on your assembly area, take the train to North Sydney or the Metro to Crows Nest (your runner email says which). There are no buses near the start, and the Harbour Bridge is closed to traffic early in the morning.
After the finish
The finish is at the Sydney Opera House forecourt, a short walk from Circular Quay station.
The course
You cross the Harbour Bridge early in the race. Enjoy it, but don't let the crowds and the views push your pace.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are on Straße des 17. Juni by the Brandenburg Gate. Use public transport (U-Bahn Bundestag or Berlin Hauptbahnhof are closest): your bib works as a ticket over race weekend.
Race morning

Arrive 60–90 minutes before your wave, as toilet queues are long. Only the official bag is allowed into the start area, and the bag drop has to be chosen when you register. Late-September mornings are chilly, so bring a throwaway layer.
The course
Flat and fast: many world records have been set here. The finish runs through the Brandenburg Gate.
Getting to the start

The start and finish are in Grant Park. Roads are closed across downtown, so take the 'L' train or walk. Every runner goes through security on Michigan Avenue: wear your bib on the front where it can be seen.
Race morning

Corrals close well before the start (in 2026 the first wave closed at 7:20 am). Aim to be in yours about 20 minutes before it closes. Only the clear bag from the expo goes to gear check. Mornings can be cold, so wear clothes you can discard.
The course

Flat and fast through many neighbourhoods. Tall buildings in the Loop can confuse GPS watches in the first kilometres, so run by feel there. The only real climb is a short rise onto Roosevelt Road just before the finish.
Getting to the start

The start is at Fort Wadsworth on Staten Island. You get there by the Staten Island Ferry plus an NYRR bus, or by an NYRR bus from Midtown Manhattan, and you choose before race day. Allow about 90 minutes or more.
Race morning

You may wait one to three hours outdoors in the start village. Bring warm throwaway layers, something to sit on and your usual breakfast. Only the official clear bag is allowed in; choose bag check or the no-bag poncho option in advance.
The course
It begins with a climb over the windy Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, so start gently. More bridge climbs follow, and the last miles up Fifth Avenue and through Central Park are the toughest part.
Getting to the start
The start is at the Bund on the Huangpu River waterfront. Roads close before sunrise and taxis are restricted, so stay within walking distance of the start or a short walk from a metro station.
Race morning
Collect your bib and race pack at the expo beforehand; it includes the bib, timing chip and race shirt. December mornings can be cool, so start in arm sleeves or a throwaway layer.
The course

Flat, heading west along Nanjing Road and past Jing'an Temple, then south along the Huangpu River. The riverside stretch after halfway has fewer spectators, so carry any gels you rely on. The finish is in the Xujiahui area (Shanghai Stadium); check your runner guide for the exact spot.
Getting to the start
The start is by the City of Arts and Sciences. Walk if you can, or take the Metro or a bus: taxis struggle with the road closures. Your bib colour tells you your start box and wave time.
Race morning
Collect your bib in person at the expo at Feria Valencia (QR code and photo ID). Bag drop must be booked in advance and places are limited. Arrive at least an hour before your wave.
The course

Flat and fast on wide boulevards, which makes it easy to start too quickly: the first kilometre should feel almost too easy. The finish is a famous blue walkway over the water in front of the City of Arts and Sciences.
Getting to the start

The start and finish are at the 1928 Olympic Stadium. Take the train or metro to Amsterdam Zuid and follow the signed walking route. Trams and buses run a limited service on race day, and parking is scarce.
Race morning
There is no bib collection on race day: collect it at the expo at RAI Amsterdam. Leave plenty of time to get through the crowds to the bag drop and your start pen.
The course
Flat, past the Rijksmuseum and Vondelpark and out along the Amstel river, where it can be windy. Use the aid stations early, and expect a cool, possibly wet October morning.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are at the Messe (exhibition grounds). U-Bahn line U4 and bus 50 stop at Festhalle/Messe. Roads around the Messe close from early morning, so avoid driving.
The finish
You finish indoors inside the Festhalle, on a red carpet with lights and music: one of the most memorable finishes in Europe.
The course

Flat and fast through the Westend, past the Old Opera and over the river Main. Late-October weather varies a lot from year to year, from near freezing to warm and windy, so check the forecast before you pack.
Getting to the start
The start is on the Champs-Élysées. Stay near a metro line and arrive early: start pens are strictly enforced, and you can only enter the pen that matches your bib.
The course

The first kilometres run downhill to Place de la Concorde: don't go out too fast. The course loops through the quieter Bois de Vincennes, then follows the Seine through several dark tunnels between about 25 and 35 km, before finishing on Avenue Foch.
After the finish
It's a long walk out of the finish area, and phones often struggle. Agree a meeting point with family and friends in advance. April weather is changeable, sometimes sunny and hot.
Getting to the start
The start is by the Colosseum and the Imperial Forums. Take Metro line B to Colosseo. Roads around Piazza Venezia close early, some from the night before.
Race morning

Expect security checks with metal detectors on the way in. Bags go in the official transparent bag with your bib number; the changing area isn't supervised, so leave nothing valuable. Collect your bib at the expo beforehand.
The course
Much of the route is on cobblestones past Rome's landmarks: wear shoes you've trained in on rough surfaces, and watch your footing when wet.
Getting to the start
The start is by Plaça d'Espanya and the Magic Fountain at the foot of Montjuïc. Take metro line L1 or L3 to Espanya, and allow extra time because the station is crowded on race morning.
The course
Mostly flat, with gentle climbs around Montjuïc and a coastal section. The long, straight early stretches make it easy to start too fast: settle into your goal pace.
Weather
March mornings are usually mild, around 10–16 °C, but the sun can get warm later in the race.
Getting to the start

The start and finish are at the Olympic Stadium on Isla de la Cartuja, across the river from the old town. Runners have found the transport from the old town confusing, so plan your route the day before.
Race morning
Arrive 45–60 minutes before the start. Bag drop is at the stadium with the bag from your race pack, a few hundred metres from the start.
The course
One of the flattest marathons in Europe, built for even pacing. Start at your goal pace and resist going faster in the first half.
Getting to the start

The race starts in the town of Marathon, 42 km from Athens. Free official buses leave from several points in central Athens early in the morning (roughly 5:30–6:45). After that, road closures make the start impossible to reach, so don't miss them.
Race morning
There is no bag drop at the start: bags are handed in beforehand, at the expo, in the official race bag. Expect a long wait in Marathon, and bring warm throwaway layers.
The course

The first 10 km or so are flat, then the road climbs, with mostly uphill running until about km 31. Don't start too fast, and train on hills. The finish is inside the marble Panathenaic Stadium. November can still be warm and humid.
Getting to the start
The start is on Wagramer Straße by UNO City (the Vienna International Centre), near the Reichsbrücke. Take U-Bahn line U1. Roads around the course close from the Friday evening before.
The finish
Recent editions finish on the Ringstraße in front of the Burgtheater, near City Hall (Rathaus); the U2 and U3 stop nearby. Check your runner guide for the bag collection point.
The course
Flat, across the Danube and around the Ringstraße and the Prater. Start at your goal pace and don't let the crowds on the bridge pull you faster.
Getting to the start

The start and finish are on Karolinenstraße by the Messe (exhibition centre). Take the U-Bahn to Messehallen (U2), Feldstraße (U3) or Stephansplatz (U1), or the S-Bahn to Sternschanze or Dammtor. Parking is limited.
Race morning

Collect your race pack at the expo on Friday or Saturday (race-day pickup only with a pre-booked slot). Arrive 1–2 hours early. The coloured dot next to your start-block letter tells you which signed route to follow; family can't enter the runners' area.
The course
Flat and fast, with big crowds. If you wear a hydration vest, keep the straps off your bib so the timing chip works.
Getting to the start
The start is on Paseo de la Castellana in central Madrid. Use the Metro: roads in the centre are closed.
The course

A tour of the city: Cibeles, Puerta de Alcalá, Gran Vía, Puerta del Sol and the Royal Palace, then out along the Manzanares river. It's rolling rather than flat, and Madrid sits about 650 m above sea level, so pace by effort.
Crowds
Gran Vía, Sol and Cibeles have the loudest support. Enjoy it, but don't let it push your pace early on.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are in Old Town Square, next to the Astronomical Clock. The old town is closed to traffic, so walk or take the metro to a nearby station.
The course

Mostly flat, crossing the Vltava many times, with Charles Bridge in the first few kilometres. There are some cobbled sections in the historic centre and on bridges, so watch your footing, especially when wet.
Pacing
The old-town start is narrow and busy. Settle into your goal pace once the field spreads out.
Getting to the start

The start and finish are on Øster Allé next to Fælledparken. The organiser recommends walking, cycling or the Metro (Trianglen, Vibenshus Runddel or Poul Henningsens Plads), and the Metro gets very busy.
Race morning

The start area opens at 7:30. Arrive at least an hour before your start to drop your bag in the runners' area, use the toilets and find your wave. At the expo, showing the email on your phone is enough to collect your bib.
The course
Flat, so pace evenly: energy spent chasing time early costs you much more at the end. Pace teams run for many target times.
Getting to the start
The start is on Leeson Street in the city centre, and the finish is nearby by the Pepper Canister Church on Mount Street. Rolling road closures apply, so walk or check public transport diversions.
Race morning
Bag drop is in Merrion Square, only in the official race bag. Allow 15–20 minutes to walk from the bag area to your start zone. Waves start from about 8:45 and are set by the finish time you entered.
The course
Mostly flat with some climbs, including the hill nicknamed Heartbreak Hill in the second half. Collect your bib at the expo at the RDS beforehand.
Getting to the start
The start is at Hans-Jochen-Vogel-Platz (formerly Coubertinplatz) in the Olympic Park. Only runners with a bib can enter the start area, and your start time is printed on your bib.
Race morning

Put your clothes in the sports bag issued with your bib (number clearly written on it) and drop it in the Olympic Hall. Larger luggage can go to a paid cloakroom. Clothes left in the start area are collected and not returned.
The finish
While the Olympic Stadium is being renovated, the finish is in the Olympic Park rather than inside the stadium. Collect your bag by 4 pm.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are at Heroes' Square, by the City Park (Városliget). A metro station is a couple of minutes' walk from the race village, and bag drop is in the race village.
Race morning
Collect your bib before race day. Arrive about an hour early: it takes time to get from the bag drop to your start zone.
The course
A loop down Andrássy Avenue and along both banks of the Danube, mostly flat with a few gentle rises. The wide riverside roads have little shade, so drink early if it's sunny.
Getting to the start

The start is on the Asian side, just before the 15 July Martyrs (Bosphorus) Bridge, so you run from Asia to Europe. Road closures are widespread on race morning: plan to use public transport, and check the organiser's transport information for the day.
The course

After the bridge, the course runs through Beşiktaş, over the Galata Bridge and along the Kennedy Avenue coastal road, finishing in Sultanahmet Square by the Blue Mosque. The bridge is long and exposed, so expect wind.
Race morning
Check the cut-off time in your runner guide (about 6 hours 20 minutes in 2025), and don't start too fast on the bridge.
Getting to the start

Recent editions started by Sea Life Porto on Via do Castelo do Queijo, on the coast in Foz, and finished at the Queimódromo at the entrance to the City Park. Check your runner guide, as the start and finish have moved between years.
Race morning
Bibs must be collected at the expo: they can't be picked up any other time. All luggage must be in a bag labelled with your race number.
The course
Mostly flat along the sea and the river Douro. Pacers with flags or balloons run times from 3:00 to 4:45.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are in Piazza del Duomo, with the start at 8:30. The old centre is closed to traffic, so walk from your hotel. Check your runner guide for the bag drop location.
The course
Essentially flat: out through the Cascine park and back into the historic centre, where the last kilometres are on wide cobblestones. Wear shoes you've tested on rough surfaces.
Cut-offs
The time limit is 6 hours, with intermediate cut-offs at halfway (3:00) and 30 km (4:15). Near the finish, tourists sometimes drift onto the course.
Getting to the start

The race starts at Villa Pisani in Stra, about 25 km west of Venice. Free official shuttles run to the start from Venezia Tronchetto and Venezia Mestre railway station; after the race, organiser boats and buses take you back.
The course

Along the Riviera del Brenta past historic villas, through Mestre and San Giuliano Park, then over the 4 km Ponte della Libertà into Venice. The last kilometres cross about 14 small bridges fitted with ramps, plus a pontoon bridge over the Grand Canal built for the race.
Weather
Morning fog over the lagoon is common, and the Ponte della Libertà is exposed to wind. The finish is on the waterfront at Riva dei Sette Martiri.
Getting to the start

The start is at Churchillplein/Schiedamsedijk, close to Blaak station (train, metro and tram). Family can't enter the start area, so say goodbye earlier. Metro stations get very busy, so allow extra time.
Race morning

Bag drop is only for runners who booked it when entering. It has been in tents on Schouwburgplein, with a size limit, so label your bag with your bib number. The start is preceded by "You'll Never Walk Alone".
The course
Flat, crossing the Erasmus Bridge early on, and finishing on the Coolsingel by City Hall, a famously loud last 500 m. Afterwards, meet family at the signed meeting points.
Getting to the start

The start is by Old Trafford stadium. Take the tram: before 9:30 get off at Old Trafford or Trafford Bar (10 minutes' walk); later, use Wharfside or Exchange Quay so you don't have to cross the course. Trams are extremely busy, so leave much more time than you think.
Race morning

Everyone enters through the E2 car park at Old Trafford. Bag drop is on Wharfside Way, in the official bag only, and closes 15 minutes before your wave. Arrive at least 45 minutes before your wave time if you're dropping a bag.
Waves
Your wave is colour-coded on your bib. You can move to a later wave on the day but not an earlier one. Family can't enter the start area, so agree a meeting point.
Getting to the start
The start is in Preston Park, a walk or short warm-up jog from Brighton station. Roads around the park close from 6:30, so get dropped off at least half a mile away and walk.
Race morning
Arrive at your allocated arrival time. Bag drop is at the start; allow plenty of time, as toilet queues are long. You can move to a later wave on the day but not an earlier one.
The course
The finish is on Hove Lawns on the seafront (older guides say Madeira Drive). The seafront sections can be windy, so bring a layer you can throw away at the start.
Getting to the start
The marathon starts in the city centre on Potterrow, by McEwan Hall, at 10:00 (the half marathon goes first at 8:00). It's point-to-point: you finish near Musselburgh, east along the coast.
Getting back

Plan your return before race day. Official finish shuttles back to the city must be booked in advance on the runners' portal. Trains stop at Musselburgh and Wallyford near the finish (buy tickets in advance), and Lothian buses run from Musselburgh. Everything is very busy.
The course
The course drops almost 90 m to sea level, so the early downhill feels deceptively easy: hold back. The second half follows the coast, which can be exposed to wind.
Getting to the start
The start is on Lidingövägen outside the 1912 Olympic Stadium in Östermalm. The race starts at midday (around 12:00, in waves), so plan your breakfast and lunch accordingly.
The course

A single loop through Djurgården, Gamla stan, Södermalm and Kungsholmen, crossing several bridges. The toughest stretches (Katarinavägen, Hornsgatan and the long climb onto the Västerbron bridge) come around the middle of the race.
The finish
You finish inside the 1912 Olympic Stadium. A midday start in late May can be warm, so drink early.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are at Rådhusplassen (City Hall Square) on the harbour, in the city centre.
The course
Along the Oslofjord and through Aker Brygge, Frogner, Vigeland Park, Bislett and Karl Johan. It's not a flat course: there are several long climbs, so pace by effort rather than by the watch.
Race morning
Start pools are based on the finish time you gave when you registered. Time limits are fairly strict, so check them in your runner guide.
Getting to the start
The start is beside the Olympic Stadium on Mäntymäentie, by the Paavo Nurmi statue, and the finish is inside the stadium. Collect your bib early (the race office is busiest late Saturday morning).
Race morning

Bag drop is at the stadium's north square: use your own closable bag and attach the tag from your bib with a tie from the race office. There's no storage for valuables except a paid service. Be at the start at least 15 minutes early.
The course
Two laps, the first one longer with an extra loop in the south of the city. Gently rolling rather than flat; the last 8 km are flat.
Getting to the start

From 2026 the start is on Sæmundargata by the University of Iceland (line up using the arch there) and the finish is on Geirsgata; earlier editions used Sóleyjargata and Lækjargata. Place yourself in the start area that matches your expected pace. Collect your bib at the expo at Laugardalshöll beforehand.
The course
Mostly flat with some gentle rises, and long stretches along the sea with few spectators and little shelter from the wind, especially in the second half.
Weather
Usually around 12 °C in August, ideal for running, but conditions change quickly. Dress in layers, and bring a cap and anti-chafe cream if it's wet.
Getting to the start
The marathon starts early in the morning (7:35 in 2026) on the 11 November Embankment by the Daugava river, next to the Old Town.
Race morning
Bag storage is at Dome Square in the Old Town, opening early on race day. It's free for marathon runners if you choose it in advance (by 30 April for 2027).
The course
Flat and fast, through the UNESCO-listed Old Town and over the bridges across the Daugava.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are on Freedom Square in the city centre. The race office, bib collection, gear check and changing tents are all on the square too.
Race morning
The marathon starts at 9:00. Gear check takes one sealed bag per runner, so don't leave bags unattended.
The course
Mostly flat. It's a smaller race, so you may run alone at times: carry your own gels and have a plan to stay focused.
Getting to the start
The marathon starts at 9:00 on Świętokrzyska Street, near the Palace of Culture and Science in the city centre. Use public transport, as roads along the course are closed.
The course
A loop through seven districts, over the Poniatowski and Gdański bridges, past the National Stadium, and along Krakowskie Przedmieście and Nowy Świat.
Race morning
Bag deposit opens at 7:30. The course closes at about 15:30 (6.5-hour limit).
Getting to the start
The start and finish are on Hlavná Street in the historic centre, in front of the DoubleTree by Hilton hotel. Arrive at the start sector in good time: you can't enter it without your bib.
Race morning

Wear your bib on your chest or on the front of a race belt, and don't fold the timing chip. Changing rooms and bag storage are in a marked building on Hlavná Street; check this year's instructions for the address.
The course
Two almost identical laps, every kilometre marked. Pacemakers run in the marathon. It's Europe's oldest marathon, first run in 1924.
Getting to the start

The start is on Slovenska cesta in the city centre and the finish is about 500 m away at Kongresni trg, so both are walkable from central hotels. Collect your bib at the expo at the GR Ljubljana exhibition centre in the days before.
The course
One flat loop (older guides describe two laps). The southern residential stretch is quiet, with little crowd support, and there are some old cobbles: plan for both.
Weather
Expect a cool start (around 7 °C) warming to the mid-teens. October is one of Ljubljana's wettest months, so bring a light rain layer.
Getting to the start

The 2026 race starts in Carcavelos, in front of NOVA School of Business & Economics, west of Lisbon (earlier editions started in Cascais). Take the Cascais line train from Cais do Sodré, and check the organiser's notices for runner trains and free travel with your bib.
The course
Point-to-point and flat, along the ocean and the Tagus river to the finish at Praça do Comércio. The coastal stretch has little crowd support and some wind.
Sun
You run with the sun in your face for much of the race: sunglasses and a cap or visor help. The closest stations to the finish are Cais do Sodré and Rossio.
The course
Two laps of a practically flat circuit that passes the city's three beaches (La Concha, Ondarreta and Zurriola) several times: one of the most scenic flat marathons in Spain.
Pacing
Because you pass the same places twice, it's easy to judge your effort: run the first lap at goal pace and save something for the second.
Race morning
Check the official runner guide for the start and finish point and bag drop; late-November weather in the Basque Country can be wet and windy.
Getting to the start

The start is at Ottoplatz by Köln-Deutz station, across the Rhine from the old town. Kit bags are handed in on race day only, on Gereonstraße in the finish area (from 7:00 until 30 minutes before your start). From there, jog across the Hohenzollern Bridge to the start as a warm-up, or take tram lines 3 or 4 from Appellhofplatz.
The finish
You finish right next to Cologne Cathedral. Food, changing tents, showers and massage are close to the kit-bag pickup.
The course
Flat, so pace evenly. The marathon starts in colour-coded blocks.
Getting to the start
The marathon starts on Montgomerylaan and finishes on Vestdijk in the centre. Eindhoven Centraal station is within walking distance of both. Some city-centre car parks are closed, so take the train.
Race morning
Bag deposit and changing are at the event site at TU/e (MetaForum). Allow extra time, as the station is very busy.
The course
Flat, through the city and surrounding areas. Friends can follow you on the official race app and cross the course at the marked bridges.
Getting to the start

The official course starts on Route de Frank-Thomas in Cologny, on the lake's east side, and finishes on the Mont-Blanc Bridge in the city centre. Stay within walking distance or on a direct transport line.
The course
One loop combining the city, the lakeside and the surrounding countryside. Gently rolling rather than flat, so pace by effort on the rises.
Race morning
Check the cut-off time in your runner guide (6 hours on the official page). May weather is usually comfortable, with a chance of showers.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are on Mythenquai by the lake, near Hafendamm Enge. The bag check (in marked railway cars) can be 500–800 m from the start, so leave time for the walk.
Race morning
Use the official clothes bag with the sticker matching your bib. Start sectors are colour-coded by expected finish time: be in yours at least 15 minutes before the start.
The course
Flat, mostly along Lake Zurich. Food and drink stations come roughly every 3.5 km.
Getting to the start

The marathon starts outside the walls of medieval Mdina, and the only practical way there is the official race bus (pre-booked when you register), which leaves Sliema very early (05:30 for the full marathon). Local buses run a reduced, changed timetable that morning.
Race morning

Bags go into vans near the start, each marked with a range of bib numbers, and are waiting about 150 m past the finish in Sliema. Leave valuables at your hotel. There's no transport back, but the finish is in Sliema, close to most hotels.
The course
Point-to-point with a net drop of almost 200 m from Mdina to the sea, but with some climbs too. The long downhill early on can ruin your legs before halfway if you go out too fast. Be ready for rain.
Getting to the start
The start is by U.S. Bank Stadium in downtown Minneapolis (6th Street and Portland Avenue), with road closures from 5 am. From 2027 the race moves to mid-October.
The course

The first 18 miles (about 29 km) follow lakes, a creek and the Mississippi and feel gentle: don't push. The hardest part is the long, steady climb up to and along Summit Avenue between about miles 20 and 23 (km 32–37).
The finish
The last mile runs downhill to the Minnesota State Capitol in St. Paul. Point-to-point, so plan your way back to Minneapolis.
Getting to the start

Take the Metro (Blue or Yellow Line) to Pentagon: it's the closest station to Runner's Village in the Pentagon's north parking lot and the start on Route 110. Arrive about two hours early for security screening, bag check and your wave.
Race morning
Waves are colour-coded (red, gold, green). You can move back to a later wave but not forward. Family can't enter Runner's Village; meet them at the Family Reunion Zone near Rosslyn Metro.
The course

The 14th Street Bridge around mile 20 (km 32) is the toughest stretch: slightly uphill, no spectators and no shade. The race ends with a short, steep climb to the Marine Corps War Memorial (Iwo Jima statue).
Getting to the start

The start is on University Avenue just north of Queen Street, near City Hall, in downtown Toronto. Take the TTC subway: roads across the course close, parking near the waterfront is limited and trains fill up quickly.
Race morning
Bag check is organised by distance and bib number: follow the signs. Bring throwaway layers (or a bin bag) for the wait, since October mornings can be cold; donated clothes go to charity.
The course
Flat, along the waterfront past Exhibition Place, Ontario Place, Harbourfront and the CN Tower. Start at goal pace and stay even.
Getting to the start
The start is in downtown Indianapolis (in 2025 it moved to West Street, south of Maryland Street), and the finish is near the Indiana Statehouse. Many hotels are close enough to walk to your corral.
Race morning

Collect your bib and the clear gear-check bag at the expo; race-day pickup only applies if you paid for it. Gear check opens at 6:30 at Washington and West streets and only accepts the clear bag. The race starts at 8:00.
The course
Flat, with lots of turns and a few small rises. The long final stretch down Meridian Street has no shade, so bring sunglasses or a cap if it's sunny.
Getting to the start

The start and finish are by the Philadelphia Museum of Art on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway. Security opens at 5 am, and you must show your bib. The two lines on the Parkway are the longest; the entrances to the southwest and north are usually shorter.
Race morning
Gear check is free but only takes the clear bag from the expo, with the tag from your bib attached. Allow time: gear-check and toilet lines inside the secure area get long.
The course

The hills come early, in Fairmount Park around miles 8–10 (km 13–16), so don't go out too fast. The second half is an out-and-back along the river to lively Manayunk and back on flat, exposed Kelly Drive, often into the wind.
Getting to the start

CIM is point-to-point, from Folsom Dam to the State Capitol in Sacramento. You must take the official race buses to the start (included in your entry): your bib won't get you through the road closures. Buses leave very early (from about 5:00); check you're on the right one.
Race morning
You can stay on the warm bus until close to the 7:00 start. The start area closes at 7:30.
The course
Gently rolling roads through small towns, finishing at the Capitol. Aid stations are frequent (17 in 2024). After 6 hours, race services can't be guaranteed.
Race morning
The race starts at 5 am in the dark, with fireworks instead of a starting gun. The sun rises around 7, so the first two hours are the coolest: use them wisely.
Heat

Humidity makes Honolulu harder than its course suggests. Slow your goal pace, drink at every station and pour water over your head and wrists. Sports drinks and gels are offered early on but become scarce later, so carry your own.
Getting there
Parking near the start at Ala Moana is limited and ride-hailing is in very high demand before dawn, so stay within walking distance if you can.
Getting to the start

The start is by the George R. Brown Convention Center downtown, where runners can wait indoors before the race. Each corral has a strictly enforced gate-closing time (A closed at 6:40 in recent years): get there at least 30 minutes before yours. You can move back to a later corral but not forward.
Race morning

Gear check is inside the convention center and only accepts the clear bag from packet pickup, with the tag from your bib. It closes at 7:00. No bags are allowed in the corrals. You need government photo ID to collect your packet.
The course
Flat and fast through downtown Houston, popular for personal bests. Pace teams run for finish times from 3 to 6 hours.
Getting to the start

The race is point-to-point, from Dodger Stadium to Century City. Free pre-race shuttles (book in your participant account) run from Century City and from downtown/Union Station in the early morning. There is no shuttle back to Dodger Stadium afterwards, so plan your return. Arrive at least 90 minutes before your start.
Race morning
Traffic around Dodger Stadium and Century City can build from 4 am. Organisers recommend Google Maps or Waze for road closures.
The course

Through Chinatown, Echo Park, Hollywood and Beverly Hills. The descent out of Dodger Stadium tempts you to start too fast, the first half has rolling hills, and there's a steady drag around miles 18–20 (km 29–32). March mornings start cool but warm up.
Getting to the start

Highway 1 is closed for the race, so runners are bused from Monterey and Carmel, starting shortly after 4 am, to the start at Big Sur Station. It's chilly while you wait: bring warm throwaway layers and gloves.
The course

The early miles are gently downhill: start slowly. The big climb is Hurricane Point (about miles 10–12, km 16–19), rising over 150 m, often into a strong wind. The steep descent to Bixby Bridge at halfway can punish your quads.
The second half

Rolling hills all the way, with a noticeable camber (sloping road) that strains ankles and knees, and a last short climb near mile 26. Pace by effort, not by the watch: this isn't a race for a personal best.
Getting to the start

The race is point-to-point, from Two Harbors to Duluth. Official buses, or the North Shore Scenic Railroad train from the DECC (limited places, with toilets on board), are the only ways to reach the start: private drop-offs aren't allowed. Buses start loading very early; you choose your pickup point in May.
Race morning
Drop your gear bag by 7:15. Toilet queues at the start are long. Clothes left at the start are donated, and mornings can be humid or foggy by the lake.
The course
Mostly flat or downhill along Lake Superior. The one real climb is Lemon Drop Hill just after mile 22 (km 35): don't attack it. In Canal Park the finish looks closer than it is, so wait to sprint.
Getting to the start
The start is on Laurier Avenue near Elgin Street, by Ottawa City Hall. Use the O-Train (Rideau or uOttawa stations), which opens at 5 am on race day; road closures start from the Friday.
Race morning
Bag check is at Lisgar Field, behind Festival Plaza. Collect your bib at the expo before race day.
Weather
Late May in Ottawa can be warm, so drink early and adjust your pace if it's hot.
Getting to the start

The start is at Queen Elizabeth Park and the finish is downtown near the Vancouver Convention Centre. Take the Canada Line to King Edward station (about 10 minutes' walk), since parking is difficult. Use the gear check, as start and finish are far apart.
The course

After a short climb out of the park and a fast early downhill, the hard part comes early: the climbs up Camosun and through Point Grey around km 8–11. Run them by effort. Don't hammer the long descent to Spanish Banks after UBC.
The second half
Stanley Park has rolling hills, and the Burrard Bridge after mile 18 (km 29) feels harder than it looks. Much of the course is exposed, so a sunny day feels warm.
Altitude
Mexico City sits at about 2,250 m. The thin air makes everything feel harder, so pace by effort, especially early, and don't chase a sea-level goal time. Arriving a few days early helps.
The course

Point-to-point, starting before sunrise at the Estadio Olímpico Universitario and finishing in the historic centre by the Zócalo, past Chapultepec Park, Paseo de la Reforma and the Angel of Independence.
Weather
Late August is the rainy season, but rain usually falls in the afternoon and mornings are clearer. Air pollution can also tire you faster than usual.
Getting to the start
The start is in Palermo, at Avenida Figueroa Alcorta and Avenida Dorrego, near the Bosques de Palermo parks.
The course
Flat and fast, known as the fastest marathon in Latin America, with a few gradual climbs and a tunnel on Avenida Sarmiento late in the race. Live bands and drummers line the route.
Weather
Spring weather in September is usually mild (around 14–19 °C) but can be windy or humid. If it's warm, slow down and use every water station.
Getting to the start

The marathon is point-to-point along the coast: in 2026 it started at 5:30 at Praia da Reserva in Barra da Tijuca and finished at Aterro do Flamengo by Marina da Glória. Plan your transport to the start the day before.
The course
Mostly flat, with the ocean on one side and the mountains on the other, along the beaches into the city. It's built for even pacing: don't go out too fast.
Heat
The early start avoids the worst of the heat, but the beachfront sections have little shade and the sun is strong. Wear a cap and sunscreen, drink at every station and slow down if it's warm.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are on the Alameda (Av. Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins) by the Palacio de La Moneda. Take the Metro to La Moneda station. There's no parking, and streets close very early.
The course
A single loop through the city along wide avenues. Largely flat, with some gentle rises in the later kilometres.
Weather
April and May mornings in Santiago are cool and usually dry; dress in a layer you can throw away at the start.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are at the Glorieta Minerva roundabout, with the start at 7:00. Streets close from Saturday midday. Some hotels are right on the start line.
Altitude
Guadalajara sits at about 1,600 m, so the air is thinner than at sea level: pace by effort. Mornings are cool, but it warms quickly later.
The course
Mostly flat to gently rolling, along Avenida López Mateos and through the historic centre past the Hospicio Cabañas, crossing the Matute Remus suspension bridge twice.
Getting to the start

The start is by Osaka Castle Park, in front of the Osaka Prefectural Office. Use public transport and the stations named in your runner guide: on race day you can't reach the start blocks from Tanimachi 4-chome station. There's no parking.
Race morning

Line-up opens at 7:45 and each block closes at its own time. Starting from a block ahead of yours means disqualification. Bag check is in tents in Osaka Castle Park; arrive dressed to run. Bring a raincoat in case of a wet wait.
The course
Mostly flat through the city. Crowd support is strongest in the first half. The finish has moved between years, so check your guide.
Getting to the start

The start is at Gwanghwamun Square in central Seoul, early in the morning (7:30 in 2026), and the finish is at the 1988 Olympic Stadium in the Jamsil Sports Complex. Roads along the course close from 5 am, so use the subway.
Race morning
Drop your bag early: the baggage trucks have been known to stop taking bags 30–45 minutes before the start. With tens of thousands of runners, the start is crowded.
The course
Flat and fast, past Gyeongbokgung Palace and Dongdaemun Design Plaza and across the Han River. Check the fine-dust (air quality) forecast in the days before.
Getting to the start
The marathon starts on Nathan Road in Tsim Sha Tsui very early in the morning. Road closures start the night before. MTR lines open earlier than usual on race day, and special buses run to the start.
The course

A tough route over highways, bridges (such as Stonecutters and Ting Kau) and through tunnels, with more climbing than most city marathons, finishing in Victoria Park in Causeway Bay. Pace by effort on the bridges.
Weather
January is cool but can be humid. Use the aid stations, and check the official course map, as the route changes between years.
Getting to the start

The marathon starts by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) very early in the morning and finishes at the Bombay Gymkhana on MG Road. Fill in the emergency contact details on the back of your bib before you arrive.
The course
Along Marine Drive, past Haji Ali and over the Bandra-Worli Sea Link and the Coastal Road, then a late climb up Peddar Road that catches many runners out: train on hills.
Heat

It starts around 20–25 °C and can pass 30 °C as the morning goes on, with high humidity. Wear light clothing, a cap and sunscreen, slow your goal pace, and sip often rather than drinking a lot at once.
Getting to the start

Recent editions started from the Race Village at the F1 Pit Building, in the middle of the night (the marathon set off at about 4:25 am in 2024), with shuttle buses from about 2:30 am. Plan your sleep and transport around that.
Heat
Expect around 26–30 °C with high humidity even before dawn. Slow your goal pace, take water and sports drink at every station and pour water over your head. Wear a cap and anti-chafe cream.
The course
Past the National Stadium, Gardens by the Bay, the Merlion and the Esplanade, finishing on the historic Padang. The time limit is 7 hours.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are at Taipei City Hall Plaza in Xinyi, next to the MRT. The full marathon starts very early (around 6:00–6:30), and the first 2 km are crowded: stay relaxed and don't weave.
The course

Mostly flat, past the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and along the riverside to Dadaocheng and Yuanshan, but bridge approaches and floodgate ramps add short climbs. The riverside section is exposed to the winter monsoon wind.
Weather
December is usually 14–20 °C, ideal for running, but drizzle is possible. A throwaway jacket or poncho at the start helps.
Getting to the start
The start is in front of Kobe City Hall near Sannomiya, by the monument to Japan's first marathon.
The course

Since 2025 the course runs west along the coast, with the sea on one side and the mountains on the other, to a turnaround near Okura Beach in Akashi, then back east. Flat and easy to run, with crowds along most of the route.
The finish

You finish at Kobe Harborland (Gaslight Street) by the harbour; the old climb over the Kobe Ōhashi Bridge onto Port Island is gone. There's no subway station right at the finish, so plan your way back. The time limit is 7 hours.
Entry
Fukuoka is an elite race: you can only enter with a fast qualifying time, and the standards change between editions. Check the current ones before planning.
The course
It starts and finishes at Heiwadai Athletic Stadium (one start group from Ōhori Park), and runs through south-west Fukuoka to Kashii and back. Very flat, built for fast times.
Race morning
Cut-offs are strict for an elite race, so make sure you can hold your pace the whole way.
Getting to the start

The marathon starts in the middle of the night (2:00 am in 2026) at Sanam Luang beside the Grand Palace, finishing there as the sun rises. Check whether the BTS Skytrain runs late for runners, as it did in 2024, or book a taxi in advance.
Heat
Even at night it's around 22–28 °C with very high humidity. Slow your goal pace, drink at every station and pour water over your head and wrists.
The course
Flat, past Victory Monument, Lumphini Park and Silom. The only real climbs are the Rama VIII Bridge and an elevated road ramp, both in the first 5 km.
Getting to the start

The marathon starts at 6:00 from ADNOC Headquarters on the Corniche. The race village opens at 5:00, with bag drop for marathon runners. Collect your race pack beforehand: there's no pickup on race day.
Race morning
Pin your bib on the front, unfolded; your start area is printed on it and you need it to get in.
The course
Flat and fast, past the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Al Bateen Palace and Qasr Al Hosn. Mid-December mornings are cool (around 16 °C at 6:00), but it warms up quickly once the sun is up.
Getting to the start
The start and finish are at Hotel Park on the Doha Corniche. The marathon starts at about 6:00, before the shorter races.
Race morning
Arrive at least 30 minutes before your start, and line up according to your expected pace.
The course
Flat, along the Corniche waterfront. Roads reopen at 1 pm (the cut-off). January mornings are mild, but the sun is strong once it rises.
Getting to the start
The new course starts and finishes at Martyrs' Square in downtown Beirut. Course maps are published by the organiser in the months before the race.
Race morning

Bags go to the baggage area in your race's gathering area; collect them promptly (unclaimed bags are donated). Leave valuables at your hotel. Keep the timing tag on the back of your bib unfolded, or you won't get a time.
The course
Through downtown and along the seafront Corniche. Late-November mornings can still be warm: use the water stations.
Getting to the start

The start has moved between years. In 2025 it was outside the Carnivore restaurant on the Southern Bypass, with the finish in Uhuru Gardens (older editions used Nyayo National Stadium). Check this year's venue.
Altitude
Nairobi sits above 1,600 m, so the air is thinner: start slower than your sea-level pace.
Weather
Mornings are cool, so wear a layer you can throw away, but it warms up quickly. Drink regularly.
Getting to the start
The start has moved between years (recent editions used Place Mohammed V and El Jadida Road), so check your runner guide. The marathon starts first, at about 7:30, and roads close across the city.
The course
Flat, along palm-lined Boulevard Moulay Youssef and the Atlantic Corniche past the Hassan II Mosque. Built for even pacing, and the crowds bring music along the way.
Weather
Late-October mornings by the ocean are usually mild, but the coast can be windy.
The course
Through the historic medina past the Koutoubia Mosque, the ramparts, the palm grove and the Menara Gardens, with views of the Atlas Mountains. Mostly flat, with some gentle climbs.
Weather
Held in late January to avoid the heat: the start is usually around 15 °C, but the sun gets strong later in the morning. Wear a cap and sunscreen.
Race morning
Check your runner guide for the start point and time (the race has traditionally started at 8:00). Water stations come about every 5 km, with sponges in between.
Getting to the start

The 2026 marathon started at 6:30 at the Orca shopping mall on Ahmadu Bello Way, ran along the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Road and finished at Eko Atlantic City (earlier editions started at the National Stadium in Surulere). Check this year's start point. Roads close for hours.
Heat
Lagos is hot and humid even early in the morning. Slow your goal pace, drink at the official water points (the only hydration on course) and cool down with water.
Cut-off
You only get a medal if you finish within the 6-hour cut-off. Runners picked up by the sweeper buses aren't eligible.
Getting to the start

The race starts at 7:00 in front of the Temple of Queen Hatshepsut on Luxor's West Bank. Race packs are collected the day before at the official hotel. Some travel packages include transport to the start.
The course
A multi-lap course on the West Bank past the Colossi of Memnon, Medinet Habu and the approach to the Valley of the Kings, and through villages.
Weather
January mornings are cool, but there's almost no shade and the desert sun gets strong: wear a cap and sunscreen and drink regularly.
Getting to the start

The start is on Batman Avenue near Rod Laver Arena, and you finish inside the Melbourne Cricket Ground with the last 400 m on the MCG turf. Use public transport: parking is limited and roads are congested. Arrive an hour before your start.
Race morning
The bag drop is at the MCG car park and opens early. Attach the strip from your bib to your bag. Don't leave anything at the St Kilda drink station: it isn't staffed for bags.
The course
Flat and fast, around Albert Park Lake and along the St Kilda beachfront. Don't burn energy in the flat early kilometres through the city. Spring weather changes quickly, so bring layers.
Getting to the start
The start, finish, bag drop and food are all at the Broadwater Parklands on Marine Parade in Southport, about 800 m from Southport station. Arrive about an hour before the early start.
The course

Flat and fast: over the Southport Bridge, south along the surf beaches to the Burleigh Heads turn, then north to Paradise Point and back to Southport. Stay relaxed in the first kilometres and don't let the crowd pull you faster.
Weather
Early July is mild winter weather (about 12–21 °C), with sunshine or the odd shower. There are 16 drink stations.
Getting to the start

The marathon starts at 6:00 on King Edward Parade in Devonport, across the harbour. Charter ferries to the start must be booked in advance in your registration (Hop cards don't work) and fill first come, first served: take an early one. Buses and trains are free with your bib.
The course

North towards Takapuna, then over the Auckland Harbour Bridge, which is steeper than it looks and often windy. Pace yourself there. Then out and back along Tamaki Drive to St Heliers, finishing in Victoria Park.
Cut-offs
There are intermediate cut-offs (including before the bridge and at St Heliers) and a 7-hour limit. Early-November mornings are cool, so bring a layer for the start.
